This is a list of the '''[[Chinese era name]]s''' used by the various [[Dynasties in Chinese history|dynasties]] and regimes in the [[history of China]], sorted by [[Chinese sovereign|monarch]].

The English renditions of the era names in this list are based on the [[Pinyin|Hanyu Pinyin]] system. However, some academic works utilize the [[Wade–Giles]] romanization. For instance, the era of ''Zhenguan'' ({{lang|zh-Hant|貞觀}}) during the reign of the [[Emperor Taizong of Tang]] is rendered as ''Chen-kuan'' in Wade–Giles.<ref name="Wade–Giles">{{cite book|last1=Winkler|first1=Dietmar|author-link=Dietmar W. Winkler|last2=Tang|first2=Li|title=Hidden Treasures and Intercultural Encounters: Studies on East Syriac Christianity in China and Central Asia|year=2009|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7f9gS40A_3IC&dq=chen-kuan&pg=PA267|page=267|isbn=9783643500458}}</ref>

==[[Republic of China]]==
{{Main|Republic of China calendar}}
{| class="wikitable"
|-
!Current Calendar
!Period of use
!Length of use
!Remark
|-
!colspan="4"|[[Republic of China]]<br/>{{small|(r. 1912–present CE)}}
|-
|[[Republic of China calendar|Minguo]]<br/>{{lang|zh-Hant|民國}}
|1912–present
|Current calendar
|Used alongside the Gōnglì {{lang|zh-Hant|公历}} ([[Gregorian calendar]]) since 1912
|-
|}

The Republic of China officially uses the Republic of China calendar. While not an era name, the Republic of China calendar is based on the era name system of Imperial China. The Republic of China calendar was the official calendar of [[mainland China]] between 1912 CE and 1949 CE, and has been in official use in [[Free area of the Republic of China|Taiwan]] since 1945 CE.
